manoj-kumar-sharma-12th-fail-ips-upsc-fo.seo_title: Manoj Kumar Sharma: UPSC rank, attempts and real 12th Fail story
manoj-kumar-sharma-12th-fail-ips-upsc-fo.answer: Manoj Kumar Sharma cleared the UPSC civil services exam on his fourth attempt with All India Rank 121. He is a 2005-batch IPS officer, Maharashtra cadre. He failed Class 12 in Morena, Madhya Pradesh, and the film 12th Fail is based on his life.

dick-fosbury-flop-laughed-at-olympic-gol.seo_title: Fosbury Flop: Dick Fosbury's high jump and 1968 Olympic gold
dick-fosbury-flop-laughed-at-olympic-gol.answer: Dick Fosbury lent his name to the Fosbury Flop in the high jump. Going over the bar head-first and backwards, he won high-jump gold at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics with an Olympic-record 2.24 metres.

steven-spielberg-rejected-by-usc-film-sc.seo_title: Did Spielberg go to USC? Rejected twice, degree at 55
steven-spielberg-rejected-by-usc-film-sc.answer: No. USC's film school rejected Steven Spielberg twice. He studied at California State College, Long Beach, left in 1968 for a Universal contract, and finished his degree there in 2002, aged 55.

vera-wang-started-her-company-at-40-stor.seo_title: Vera Wang at 40: Vogue, a missed Olympic team and her first salon
vera-wang-started-her-company-at-40-stor.answer: Vera Wang opened her first bridal salon in New York in 1990, at about 40. Before that she missed the 1968 U.S. Olympic skating team and spent 17 years at Vogue.

lijjat-papad-seven-women-80-rupees-story.seo_title: Lijjat Papad turnover 2026, founders and ₹80 start
lijjat-papad-seven-women-80-rupees-story.answer: Lijjat Papad's annual turnover is reported at more than ₹1,600 crore. Seven women in Girgaum, Mumbai, started it on 15 March 1959 with ₹80 borrowed money, and about 45,000 women now co-own it.

paras: As an accountant, the number I keep coming back to is the ₹80. Adjusted for India's consumer price inflation, it is worth roughly ₹7,400 in today's money. That is less than many people spend on a phone. It was never the capital that built Lijjat.

What built it was compounding. Sales in the first year were just over ₹6,000. Reports now put turnover at about ₹1,600 crore. That is roughly 27 lakh times larger, which works out to sales growing about 26% a year, every year, for more than six decades. Even after removing inflation, real growth was about 18% a year. Very few Indian businesses of any kind have sustained that for so long.

One caution when reading these figures: ₹1,600 crore is turnover, not profit, and it is shared across about 45,000 members. That is roughly ₹3.6 lakh of sales per member each year, before the cost of flour, spices and packing. Lijjat's real achievement is not one big number. It is thousands of steady, modest earnings that the women own outright.

ray-kroc-52-milkshake-mixer-salesman-bui.seo_title: How old was Ray Kroc when he met the McDonald brothers?
ray-kroc-52-milkshake-mixer-salesman-bui.answer: Ray Kroc was 52 when he met Dick and Mac McDonald in San Bernardino in 1954, while selling milkshake mixers. He opened his first McDonald's in 1955 and bought the brothers out for $2.7 million in 1961.

paras: In 1961 Ray Kroc paid the McDonald brothers $2.7 million for their rights, about $28 million in today's dollars. Before that deal, the brothers took just 0.5% of their franchisees' sales. That is a small share of a fast-growing business, and Kroc's own cut was only 1.4%.

The money was really made in property. Harry Sonneborn's plan had the company own or lease the land and rent it to franchisees, so rent arrived every month whatever happened to burger prices. When McDonald's listed in 1965 at $22.50 a share, about $224 today, investors were buying a property business as much as a restaurant chain.

oldest-olympic-medal-winners-athletes-wh.seo_title: Oldest Olympic medal winners and gold medallists ever
oldest-olympic-medal-winners-athletes-wh.answer: The oldest Olympic medallist is Sweden's Oscar Swahn, who won shooting silver at the 1920 Olympics aged 72. He is also the oldest gold medallist, at 64 in 1912.

marvel-bankruptcy-1996-to-disney-4-billi.seo_title: Marvel bankruptcy 1996: why it went bust and what saved it
marvel-bankruptcy-1996-to-disney-4-billi.answer: Marvel filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 1996 after the comics and trading-card boom collapsed. It merged with Toy Biz in 1998, financed its own films, made Iron Man in 2008, and Disney bought it for about $4 billion in 2009.

paras: In 1998 Marvel reportedly offered Sony almost all its film characters for $25 million, about $48 million in today's dollars. Eleven years later Disney paid about $4 billion for the company, 160 times that offer, or nearly $5.8 billion today.

What changed in between was not the characters but who kept the profit. Selling film rights for a fixed fee turns a character into a one-off payment. In 2005 Marvel instead borrowed $525 million against its remaining rights to make its own films. Iron Man earned about $585 million, roughly $850 million today, and that income went to Marvel.

ms-dhoni-ticket-collector-kharagpur-to-w.seo_title: Was MS Dhoni a ticket collector? Kharagpur to World Cup 2011
ms-dhoni-ticket-collector-kharagpur-to-w.answer: Yes. MS Dhoni worked as a travelling ticket examiner for South Eastern Railway at Kharagpur, reportedly from 2001 to 2004. In 2011 he scored 91 not out in the World Cup final and hit the winning six.

sundar-pichai-slept-on-living-room-floor.seo_title: Sundar Pichai's childhood in Chennai: house, family, struggles
sundar-pichai-slept-on-living-room-floor.answer: Sundar Pichai grew up in a modest house in Chennai shared with tenants. His family slept on the living room floor, queued for water in a drought and waited five years for a phone.

jadav-payeng-forest-man-of-india-molai-f.seo_title: Molai forest: Jadav Payeng, the Forest Man of India (Assam)
jadav-payeng-forest-man-of-india-molai-f.answer: Jadav Payeng, the Forest Man of India, is from Assam. Since 1979 he has planted Molai forest on a Brahmaputra sandbar near Jorhat; it now covers about 1,360 acres (about 550 hectares).

paras: The famous ₹10,000 sounds tiny, but 1981 prices were very different. Adjusted for inflation, it is worth about ₹2.1 lakh today. That is real savings for a young family, and Sudha Murty still kept ₹250 back for emergencies. That habit tells you more about how Infosys was run than the headline number does.

The growth is the real lesson. In 1999, the year it listed on Nasdaq, Infosys crossed US$100 million in revenue. It now reports about US$20 billion, roughly 200 times more. That is about 23% growth a year for 26 years, at a company already large when the run began.
money.note: Inflation uses India's consumer price index from the World Bank (series FP.CPI.TOTL, to 2025). Figures are rounded. General education, not financial advice.

paras: Sunil Mittal's ₹20,000 from 1976 is worth about ₹6.3 lakh in today's money. That is a serious sum for an 18-year-old, but it is roughly what a small trader might put into a shop today, not venture capital.

As an accountant, what stands out is that it was borrowed, from his father. Borrowed money has to come back, which forces a business to sell something early. A bicycle-parts workshop does exactly that: small, steady orders that pay the loan, long before anything as ambitious as a phone network.
money.note: Inflation uses India's consumer price index from the World Bank (series FP.CPI.TOTL, to 2025). Figures are rounded. General education, not financial advice.

paras: Ronald Wayne's $800 from 1976 is worth about $4,400 in today's dollars. Including the later $1,500, he received $2,300, about $12,700 today. Set against estimates of more than $400 billion for a 10% stake now, it looks like the worst trade in history.

The accountant's view is different. In a general partnership, each partner can be personally liable for the business's debts. Jobs had just borrowed $15,000 for parts, about $83,000 today, and Wayne had a house and savings that creditors could reach. He was not selling a share of Apple's future. He was buying protection from a debt he could not control.
